gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-mende-kikak: Neon looks drawn with a fixed-width nib, vibrant and spaced out, with tall lowercase like stamped metal. And Noto Sans Mende Kikakui handles the quieter work, letting daylight into every curve while its lowercase stands tall against the capitals.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-meroitic: Glowing and vibrant, Neon looks like bent pipe-cleaner strokes, every letter the same width. Noto Sans Meroitic is the approachable counterweight, with see-through openings and lowercase filling the line.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-modi: Glowing tubes of single-width line. Noto Sans Modi gives that heading a modern sans-serif partner, with daylight inside every curve and a lowercase that sits close to capital height, so the two feel related yet clearly different.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-mono: Neon turns every curve at full width, with no pressure swell at the corner, and spaces its letters openly. But Noto Sans Mono brings sturdy, tall lowercase and generous curve openings, so the text feels weighty beside that glow.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-mro: Noto Sans Mro reads dense and tall through the middle of its words, with large entrances into each letter's inner space. Neon does the glowing bent-steel-rod display work; this sans handles the steady text.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-multani: Glowing rods, no hairlines in sight. Neon is best at bold, full-width stroke connections that catch the eye, while Noto Sans Multani does its best work as a modern sans with a lofty x-height and a wide gap at the e's terminal.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Vibrant from the first letter, Neon keeps bold-looking and light-looking strokes from ever mixing inside a word. But its strongest quality is contrast with Noto Sans Nabataean, whose lowercase stands almost cap-tall with wide-open s curves.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-nag-mundari: Neon gives its t a crossbar and stem of one width, and the whole glowing heading follows that logic of uniform line. Noto Sans Nag Mundari would read smoothly over pages, its lowercase rivaling the capitals.
